- Shredded, disintegrated pith with intact vascular strands
- Tan/brown overall coloration

Top candidates: **Charcoal_stalk_rot** (tiny black sclerotia on vascular strands, grey/charred interior), **Diplodia_stalk_rot** (small black pycnidia, rotted tan/brown pith), **Anthracnose_stalk_rot** (black rind discoloration). Let me check reference images.
The Charcoal rot reference (bottom-right) shows a very similar reddish-tan shredded stalk. Let me check a few more candidates to confirm.

Fusarium shows more ear-focused symptoms, Physoderma stalk rot shows dark/black nodes, and Bacterial stalk rot shows water-soaked collapse. Let me view a few more references to confirm Charcoal stalk rot vs Anthracnose.

The leaf disease references (Gray leaf spot, NCLB, Anthracnose leaf spot) are clearly different from the test image. My analysis is focused on stalk rots.

**Summary of evidence:**

The test image shows a longitudinal split of a corn stalk with:
- Completely shredded, disintegrated pith leaving only fibrous vascular strands
- Tan to reddish-brown coloration
- Many small dark dots (putative sclerotia) scattered throughout the tissue
- No pink/red coloration (rules out Fusarium/Gibberella)
- No shiny black external rind discoloration (rules out Anthracnose stalk rot)
- No intact node with black snapping (rules out Physoderma stalk rot)
- No slimy/mushy tissue with foul odor (rules out Bacterial stalk rot)

The **Charcoal_stalk_rot** reference image (bottom-right panel) shows a nearly identical reddish-tan shredded stalk with fibrous vascular strands — matching the test image very closely. The small dark dots in the test image are consistent with tiny black spherical sclerotia characteristic of Charcoal stalk rot (*Macrophomina phaseolina*).
